evidence: src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts: CycleCountService (constructor, count, openDiscrepancies) injects PrismaService directly and calls this.prisma.stockCount.create and this.prisma.stockCount.findMany instead of using a persistence table/repository abstraction.

src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts: ReceivingService (constructor, receive, pick, item, bin) reaches persistence through the table abstractions ItemTable and BinTable and operates through the domain abstractions Bin, Item, and StockError.

src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts: CycleCountService.count and CycleCountService.openDiscrepancies bypass the domain model (Bin) to operate on raw primitives and Prisma records, and duplicate the discrepancy calculation (counted !== expected and counted - expected) in both methods.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module src/business/services does not maintain a consistent persistence boundary or abstraction across its files. In src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts, ReceivingService (via constructor, receive, pick, item, and bin) accesses persistence through table repository abstractions (ItemTable and BinTable) and enforces domain rules through domain abstractions (Bin, Item, and StockError). In contrast, in src/business/services/CycleCountService.ts, CycleCountService injects the ORM client wrapper PrismaService directly in its constructor and executes raw Prisma queries (this.prisma.stockCount.create in count and this.prisma.stockCount.findMany in openDiscrepancies), reaching persistence around the table/repository boundary and bypassing the domain abstractions. Additionally, CycleCountService writes out the discrepancy rule (comparing counted and expected and computing counted - expected) in two places: count and openDiscrepancies.

violations.message: CycleCountService (constructor, count, openDiscrepancies) reaches persistence directly via PrismaService (this.prisma.stockCount.create and this.prisma.stockCount.findMany) instead of a table/repository abstraction like BinTable and ItemTable used in src/business/services/ReceivingService.ts, bypasses the Bin domain abstraction, and duplicates the discrepancy calculation across count and openDiscrepancies.
